title: Matrix linear maps

review.history: source gap; no origin or priority assertions

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Transform a vector and its surrounding grid with the same matrix rule.
meaning: A 2 by 2 real matrix combines its columns according to the input coordinates. The two row calculations produce output coordinates. The linear map fixes the origin and can stretch, shear, rotate, reflect or collapse shapes.

signature.mappedX: ax+by; the first coordinate and primary numeric output
signature.determinant: ad-bc; zero means no unique inverse
signature.area: |ad-bc|, area of the mapped unit square

conditions: Keep the declared matrix row order and column-vector input.
The matrix and vector dimensions must agree.
Linear maps fix zero and preserve vector addition and real scalar multiplication.
The mapped unit-square area is |ad-bc|; zero determinant is a valid collapse.
definition.domain_notes: The formal matrix rule is defined on all of R². The UI restricts coefficients to [-2,2] and displayed input components to [-3,3]; this viewing box is not itself a vector space. No translation, nonlinear warp, arbitrary matrix dimensions or inverse computation is implemented. Singular matrices remain valid maps. Stories declare physical coordinate units separately.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; worked properties are author-derived for stated assumptions. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.pronunciation: Matrix linear maps in real two-dimensional coordinates
grammar.formation_rule: output=mappedX=a*x+b*y; mappedY=c*x+d*y; determinant=signedArea=a*d-b*c; area=abs(determinant); inverseExists=(determinant!=0); inputNorm=hypot(x,y); mappedNorm=hypot(mappedX,mappedY).
grammar.precedence: Multiply corresponding entries before adding or subtracting. Ordered coordinates and matrix entries retain their stated positions.
